best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Competitor Lobbying Intensifies NY Medical Advertising Standards
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a healthcare directory and appointment platform with embedded telehealth booking, making state medical advertising and anti-kickback compliance material exposures distinct from pure-play virtual care competitors. Four telehealth operators filed federal lobbying disclosures in May 2026 addressing telehealth regulatory topics, signaling sector-wide mobilization around state-level prescribing, advertising, and referral economics. New York's medical advertising rules and anti-kickback statute enforcement create operational risk for marketplace platforms that connect patients to telehealth providers through financial incentives or featured placement. Regulatory affairs leadership should monitor whether competitor positions on telehealth access and referral economics influence New York's enforcement priorities.

Subject: Competitor Telehealth Lobbying in NY, Advertising & Anti-Kickback Risk Dear [Public Policy Head], Four telehealth competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures last month addressing telehealth regulatory topics. Given Zocdoc's directory-and-booking model in New York, your government affairs team should assess whether competitor positions on prescribing incentives or provider placement economics signal emerging enforcement targets. Would a 15-minute call on Thursday work to discuss state-specific exposure mapping? Best,
[Rep Name]

best_narrative.headline: Spring Health: Competitors File Federal Telehealth Lobbying
best_narrative.body: Spring Health operates as a pure-play mental health platform embedded in employer benefit designs, creating direct exposure to state behavioral health licensing requirements and Medicaid mental health reimbursement rules across NY, CA, and FL. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include state-level asynchronous prescribing restrictions, licensing reciprocity barriers, and plan network adequacy standards that shape in-network provider qualification. Competitors have recently filed federal telehealth lobbying disclosures, signaling intensified advocacy activity around telehealth scope and reimbursement policy. This competitor mobilization typically precedes state legislative pushes that affect employer plan compliance and network composition standards.
